title: Your Credit Card Became a Coupon Book
narration_text: Dave opened a premium card. Then the card handed him a homework assignment. Fifteen dollars for coffee—only this month. Twenty dollars for streaming—if you remember Tuesday. Ten dollars at a store Dave never uses. Chad calls it free money. Points Monk pulls out a calendar. If a credit changes what you buy, it isn't saving; it's steering. Count only credits you would have used anyway. Then subtract the annual fee. The card isn't a coupon book you must finish. Real value first. Credits second. Flex last.
topic_basis: 2026 premium-card trend: rising annual fees and increasingly complex coupon-book-style credits; video uses unnamed illustrative values rather than current issuer-specific terms.
